# RAVE2 Buddy

> Buddy is the local web menu and control plane for a RAVE2 board: an x86 host
> carrying an AMD Versal adaptive SoC on PCIe. It exposes an HTTP API on port
> 80 that programs the Versal, manages storage and networking, drives audio
> hardware, installs applications, and applies RAUC system updates.

Important notes before you act:

- **The API has no authentication.** It runs as root on port 80, bound to all
  interfaces. Every endpoint is reachable unauthenticated, including reboot,
  power off, BIOS flash writes, Versal programming, and an interactive shell.
  The one restriction is that state-changing requests are refused with `403`
  when `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` marks them cross-site, which blocks a
  drive-by from a browser but does not affect a direct caller.
- Long-running work is asynchronous: `POST /api/run/<action>` returns a
  `job_id`, and progress streams from `GET /api/stream/<job_id>` as Server-Sent
  Events terminated by `event: status` / `data: exited:<returncode>`.
- A single `flock` on `/run/lock/rave-bulk-operation.lock` serialises
  operations that write flash or repartition storage. Endpoints that would
  corrupt an in-flight operation return HTTP `409`. Back off and retry; never
  work around it.
- `GET` endpoints are read-only and safe, except `GET /api/rauc-status` and
  `GET /api/browse?source=ubuntu`, which mount filesystems.

## Docs

- [Agent orientation](/AGENTS.md): what the board is, safe versus destructive
  operations, where the source of record lives, and platform gotchas. Read
  this first.
- [HTTP API reference](/api.md): every endpoint, grouped by functional area,
  with request fields, response keys, exact error strings and side effects.

## Live state

- [/api/tools/version](/api/tools/version): which Versal toolchain release is
  selected and which is actually in effect
- [/api/hw-server/status](/api/hw-server/status): whether a Vivado hardware
  server is running, at which release, and on which addresses
- [/api/vivado/status](/api/vivado/status): which toolchain releases are
  installed under `/opt/tools`
- [/api/rauc-status](/api/rauc-status): A/B slot state and per-slot versions
  (note: mounts the inactive slot to read it)
- [/api/boot-default](/api/boot-default): what the board boots by default
- [/api/storage-status](/api/storage-status): bulk storage health and free space
- [/api/support-logs](/api/support-logs): how much operation history the board
  has recorded (the archive itself, `/api/support-logs/download`, can be
  hundreds of megabytes — do not fetch it casually)
- [/api/versal/luns/scan](/api/versal/luns/scan): the Versal's current UFS LUN
  layout, capacity and whether provisioning is still permitted (read-only, but
  resets the Versal to read it)
- [/api/network/services](/api/network/services): network technologies,
  services and interfaces
- [/api/board-test/status](/api/board-test/status): hardware test results
- [/api/localization](/api/localization): keyboard layout, system language, and
  which locales are installed

## Optional

- [Main menu](/): the human-facing web UI
- [Board test page](/board-test)
- [App store](/app-store)
- [Audio controls](/audio) and [developer view](/audio/developer)
- [Vivado installer](/vivado-install)
- [Localisation](/localisation): keyboard layout and language. Append `?lang=`
  to any page to override the display language for one request.
